you-win-subtitle: Your machine has successfully created the desired products.
message-please-rename-solution: Please enter a new name for this solution:

refined-gold.before-0: Well, this is an odd first project. I feel like someone's having a laugh at my expense.
refined-gold.before-1: Why, were you asked to create the Philosopher’s Stone?
refined-gold.before-4: Yes. Apparently there’s an old Van Tassen lead mine, and wouldn’t it be better if it produced gold instead of lead?
refined-gold.before-6: Sounds wonderful. Time to put your University degree to the test!
refined-gold.after-2: Well, at least it’s finished with now.
refined-gold.after-3: Like asking a fish if it can swim!
refined-gold.after-4: You're taking this remarkably poorly, Anataeus.
refined-gold.after-5: I was expecting a challenge, that’s all.
refined-gold.after-6: Sounds like you want a chance to show off.
refined-gold.after-7: I’m not sure I’d go that far.

face-powder.before-0: Have you seen the Lady Van Tassen recently?
face-powder.before-2: Did you notice how pale her face is?
face-powder.before-3: Oh, she's well known for her pallor. Why, did someone ask you to do something about it?
face-powder.before-4: Armand himself did. It seems it’s gotten worse lately. People are whispering about her health.
face-powder.before-6: The Lady hasn’t had an easy time of things. I’d hate to see her slandered on top of it all.
face-powder.after-0: This should make the Lady’s face look less pale. Though it’s quite a superficial solution.
face-powder.after-1: Who can really say what troubles the Lady Van Tassen? It’s not for us to know.
face-powder.after-2: Have you ever heard her speak? She didn’t say a word during the dinner I went to.
face-powder.after-3: I remember her speaking to me once or twice when I was a child.
face-powder.after-4: Odd. Just another one of the many Van Tassen mysteries, I suppose.
face-powder.after-5: One gets used to them after a while.

waterproof-sealant.before-0: Do you know much about ships, Concordia?
waterproof-sealant.before-1: Our merchant fleet delivers goods from overseas about once a month. Why?
waterproof-sealant.before-2: Captain Gelt told me they used to have some kind of substance they put on the hulls so they don’t rot.
waterproof-sealant.before-3: I don’t know anything about it. Have you ever been on a ship?
waterproof-sealant.before-5: Not at all. It soudns ghastly! Being tossed around on the ocean, then getting eaten by sea monsters.
waterproof-sealant.before-6: I’m not sure all sea voyages are like that.
waterproof-sealant.after-0: With this sealant ready, the fleet should soon be ready to set sail again and bring back— well, whatever it brings.
waterproof-sealant.after-1: They’re loaded with all kinds of things. Cloth, pottery, mineral ores, rare herbs... strange stones.
waterproof-sealant.after-4: I’m not sure. Those contracts were drawn up centuries ago.
waterproof-sealant.after-5: I doubt even Armand knows the details.

hangover-cure.before-0: If I’d known I was to be tasked with curing a hangover…
hangover-cure.before-1: Oh, I bet I know who asked you for that. It was Captain Gelt, wasn’t it?
hangover-cure.before-3: It would be good for him to be at least somewhat functional in the mornings.
hangover-cure.before-4: Yes, seems prudent for the head of security for the entire House to not be totally incapacitated on a regular basis.
hangover-cure.after-0: There are days when I could use such a cure myself.
hangover-cure.after-2: What? This isn’t for me, Anataeus. If you get caught–
hangover-cure.after-4: My amazing hangover cure… is water!
hangover-cure.after-6: Captain Gelt has no idea, but apparently he loves it. Works wonders, he says.
hangover-cure.after-8: Also, I’ll never trust an alchemist again.

airship-fuel.before-0: Captain Gelt asked for something to put in the Van Tassen airship. Apparently it’s out of fuel?
airship-fuel.before-2: First time I’ve heard someone say “that old thing” in reference to an airship…
airship-fuel.before-3: The last time I remember the airship in the air was the celebration for Frederick’s birth.
airship-fuel.before-4: Clearly Frederick disappointed his grandfather so much they never took it out again.
airship-fuel.before-5: Ha. More likely it’s simply been out of fuel this whole time.
airship-fuel.before-6: The whole time? Are you serious?
airship-fuel.before-7: After the old Head Alchemist died we had an “interim” one for a while who was… not great.
airship-fuel.after-0: Simple enough. Now the Van Tassen airship can take to the skies again!
airship-fuel.after-1: Sure, as long as we can find someone to pilot it.
airship-fuel.after-2: Doesn’t seem too complicated. How about me?
airship-fuel.after-3: How about Captain Gelt? Or Frederick?
airship-fuel.after-4: That’s a disturbing thought… maybe we should pretend the airship is still out of fuel.

precision-machine-oil.before-2: Apparently Armand arranged for Frederick to go on a date with a young lady from another House.
precision-machine-oil.before-4: And now I have to make some machine oil.
precision-machine-oil.before-6: For the observatory. Frederick tried to take her there, but everything was rusted solid.
precision-machine-oil.before-8: Even better? Clara, the young lady, is from House Soria.
precision-machine-oil.before-9: He was probably hoping to prove our observatory is just as good as theirs.
precision-machine-oil.before-10: Oh, she must’ve been tremendously impressed all around.
precision-machine-oil.after-0: Well, Frederick’s dates at the observatory ought to go better now. Maybe he and Clara could have a do-over.
precision-machine-oil.after-1: I don’t think it works like that.
precision-machine-oil.after-2: Do you see any other choices?
precision-machine-oil.after-3: For Clara Soria? I believe House Colvan has a young man around Frederick’s age.
precision-machine-oil.after-4: Maybe that’s what Armand is trying to prevent, no?
precision-machine-oil.after-5: Quite likely. Pity he has only Frederick to work with.
precision-machine-oil.after-6: One can only play the game with the pieces one has.

health-tonic.before-0: Do you know exactly how old Armand is?
health-tonic.before-1: Both he and the Lady are rather advanced in age.
health-tonic.before-2: And Frederick is the only possible heir?
health-tonic.before-3: As Armand’s only surviving grandson, he would be difficult to oppose.
health-tonic.before-4: There are some other claimants from distant branches of the family, but they’re weak.
health-tonic.before-6: Promise not to tell anyone, but I was asked to make a tonic to assist in regulating an irregular heartbeat.
health-tonic.before-7: Oh Armand… hopefully he’s set up everything for an orderly succession of power after he’s gone.
health-tonic.before-8: Let’s not get too ahead of ourselves. I do intend to keep him healthy.
health-tonic.after-0: There, that should do it. One healthy-ish patriarch for the House Van Tassen, as ordered.
health-tonic.after-4: I do think it’s good if he stays alive.
health-tonic.after-5: After all, he pays for everything around here.
health-tonic.after-6: You’d do well to show a little more appreciation for your House.

stamina-potion.before-0: “A little boost at the necessary time.”
stamina-potion.before-2: “A little boost at the necessary time,” is how he put it…
stamina-potion.before-6: Particularly: He wonders if Frederick will be able to produce an heir.
stamina-potion.before-8: I’m to make him a potion that will…
stamina-potion.before-9: …give him a boost at the necessary time, I get it.
stamina-potion.before-10: That’s not so unusual, really. Stamina potions have long been used for such purposes.
stamina-potion.before-11: It’s not making it that’s the issue for me. It’s thinking about it.
stamina-potion.before-12: You should know better than to use your imagination in cases like this.
stamina-potion.after-0: I hope Frederick enjoys that potion… ugh.
stamina-potion.after-1: Armand must believe Frederick’s marriage is close at hand.
stamina-potion.after-2: Really? Really? Will it be the young lady from House Soria?
stamina-potion.after-4: How exciting! The city would celebrate for days. The union of House Van Tassen and House Soria…
stamina-potion.after-5: As Provisioner, you’d have a lot of work to do.
stamina-potion.after-6: Yes, but it would be for a wedding! It would be quite fun.
stamina-potion.after-7: You arrange the party in the streets, I arrange the party in the sheets.

hair-product.before-0: This is not the best use of my time.
hair-product.before-1: The patriarch has personally requested it.
hair-product.before-3: As heir, Frederick must make a public appearance in the battle. Otherwise, it may be a problem for the family’s honor.
hair-product.before-4: I get that part. It’s the part about his hair needing to be styled perfectly that I don’t understand.
hair-product.before-6: Precisely, that’s why his hair gel needs to be extra strong.
hair-product.before-7: Do you even understand what I’m saying right now?
hair-product.before-8: This is how the Houses work, Anataeus. The way things look is very important.
hair-product.before-9: Maybe even more important than the way things are.
hair-product.before-10: I’m starting to learn that, yes.
hair-product.after-0: This ought keep Frederick’s hair solidly in place, even if he wanders into a cyclone.
hair-product.after-1: Excellent, I’ll have this sent to his personal staff immediately.
hair-product.after-2: Here’s hoping his well-styled hair helps him in the battle.
hair-product.after-3: He won’t enter the fight, that would be madness!
hair-product.after-4: He just needs to be out in the street for a little while so people see him.
hair-product.after-5: Will he make a little speech or something?
hair-product.after-7: He will hold up his sword. That should be enough to inspire the soldiers.
hair-product.after-8: I’ll take your word for it.

rocket-propellant.before-0: Shouldn’t they have stayed their attack by now?
rocket-propellant.before-1: Hm… perhaps they need a little more prompting.
rocket-propellant.before-2: I had the rockets brought out of storage, but much of the propellant has leaked away.
rocket-propellant.before-3: When was the last time they were used?
rocket-propellant.before-4: Long before either of you were born.
rocket-propellant.before-5: Well, it’s no problem. I’ll just make a new propellant.
rocket-propellant.before-6: I’m certain that’ll be more powerful than what you had before anyway.
rocket-propellant.after-0: I’m eager to see how the rockets perform.
rocket-propellant.after-1: The din and the smoke is always quite a sight. A rocket barrage should give them a good fright!
rocket-propellant.after-2: I hope it convinces them to stop advancing.
rocket-propellant.after-3: Oh yes, they’ll regret not stopping earlier.
rocket-propellant.after-4: It’s taken us long enough to organize this response.
rocket-propellant.after-5: But! Now that we have, the full might of House Van Tassen will bear down on them.
rocket-propellant.after-6: That will put a stop to their advance.

mist-of-incapacitation.before-0: Wait. The airship dock is lost now too?
mist-of-incapacitation.before-1: It seems they’re moving quite fast… faster than we anticipated.
mist-of-incapacitation.before-2: This is absurd. Don’t we outnumber them?
mist-of-incapacitation.before-4: If this keeps happening, won’t we lose the war?
mist-of-incapacitation.before-5: Come now, it’s hardly a war.
mist-of-incapacitation.before-7: I’ve explained it. It’s best understood as— say, a kind of diplomacy.
mist-of-incapacitation.before-9: I’ll do it, then. I’ll ensure that House Colvan regrets every building they take.
mist-of-incapacitation.after-0: These phials contain a vapor that makes areas inaccessible for a time.
mist-of-incapacitation.after-3: Not very honorable. I doubt Armand would be pleased.
mist-of-incapacitation.after-4: Do you have better ideas? We’ve been struggling to catch up this whole time!
mist-of-incapacitation.after-5: Nonsense. We’re making a good show of our defense while we wait for House Colvan to respond to our message.
mist-of-incapacitation.after-6: A truce will be negotiated soon enough.
mist-of-incapacitation.after-7: Won’t the terms be more favorable if we push back harder?
mist-of-incapacitation.after-8: The terms will be favorable either way. Armand is a masterful negotiator.
mist-of-incapacitation.after-9: It’s how we built this House into what it is today.

explosive-phial.before-0: I’ve got an idea for a new weapon— something simple that even the House staff could use.
explosive-phial.before-1: The staff? Those who haven’t been bestowed a sword certainly shouldn’t be given any other weapon.
explosive-phial.before-2: But what if House Colvan doesn’t stand down? What if our soldiers can’t hold the line against them?
explosive-phial.before-3: You’re being foolish. A message will arrive any moment now.
explosive-phial.before-4: You keep saying that, and yet—
explosive-phial.before-5: Besides, if there is fighting indoors, the damage to the property would be extremely unfortunate.
explosive-phial.before-6: If Colvan breach the perimeter, won’t the consequences be much worse?
explosive-phial.after-0: There, a phial of fire. Able to be thrown by anyone— even those with no training!
explosive-phial.after-1: I can’t imagine the Captain enjoying that thought.
explosive-phial.after-2: Oh, no, he absolutely hates the idea.
explosive-phial.after-4: Shouldn’t we take every measure possible to ensure our victory?
explosive-phial.after-5: Are you sure this improves our chances?
explosive-phial.after-6: I don’t know. Maybe not. I feel like I have to try everything.

armor-filament.before-0: Captain, what are you doing in that ancient armor?
armor-filament.before-1: Isn’t it obvious? I must lay down my life in battle.
armor-filament.before-2: I have to take responsibility for this situation somehow…
armor-filament.before-3: But that’s such an old set! We should get you something more up to date from the armory.
armor-filament.before-4: No, no. If I must be seen on the streets, I want to look like the heroes of old.
armor-filament.before-5: The first rocket would be your end!
armor-filament.before-6: If you insist on this set, let me at least reinforce it with some armor filament.
armor-filament.after-0: There may yet be hope. Perhaps I will single-handedly turn the tide of the battle.
armor-filament.after-2: What circumstances. A total offensive like this hasn’t happened in generations. Centuries!
armor-filament.after-4: I swore to defend House Van Tassen for life… I thought that would be a very long time…
armor-filament.after-5: No matter what happens, you will be remembered, Captain.

courage-potion.before-0: Perhaps the Colvan message was mistaken…
courage-potion.before-2: It could still be retracted! An error by a scribe or page… the wrong letter sent…
courage-potion.before-3: I’m sorry to say I think that rather unlikely.
courage-potion.before-4: Stay here a little while longer, Captain. I’ll make you a potion of courage. Something to inflame your blood with the fighting spirit.
courage-potion.before-5: Thank you, Anataeus. That’s kind of you.
courage-potion.after-0: Do you think the courage potion will work? It seems difficult to contradict the habits of a lifetime.
courage-potion.after-1: It will, after a fashion. The potion I gave him is mostly alcohol.
courage-potion.after-2: Glad to see you haven’t lost your willingness to toy with the poor Captain, even in these dire straits.
courage-potion.after-3: It’s not toying. Not this time.
courage-potion.after-4: If honor demands that he lay down his life, I want him to feel comfortable, at least, and most like himself.
courage-potion.after-5: That’s touching, in an odd sort of way.

surrender-flare.before-1: Gelt made his sacrifice, the soldiers are fleeing, and I have word from Armand himself that we’re to change the signal light on the tower to pale green.
surrender-flare.before-2: Armand is better at treaties than he is at battles. There’s hope yet after the surrender.
surrender-flare.before-3: I hate this. I did everything I could!
surrender-flare.before-4: If it hadn’t been for Captain Gelt’s tepid strategies.
surrender-flare.before-5: And Armand’s stubborn insistence on keeping “honor.”
surrender-flare.before-6: And Frederick’s inability to do anything…
surrender-flare.before-7: But the future remains to be seen.
surrender-flare.before-8: We were defeated so easily! I can’t believe this! I got here just a few months ago, and the first major event is our surrender to another House?
surrender-flare.before-9: I’ve been here my whole life and have never witnessed something like this.
surrender-flare.after-0: So what’s supposed to happen now?
surrender-flare.after-1: I’m not sure. We have negotiations?
surrender-flare.after-5: What good is my skill if I couldn’t change anything? Why did I go through the trouble?
surrender-flare.after-6: Now’s not the time for a big, philosophical, soul-searching reverie.

chapter-1-intro.name: Van Tassen’s New Alchemist
chapter-1-intro.dialogue-2: Armand kept going through his old stories about honor and righteousness.
chapter-1-intro.dialogue-3: The Lady Van Tassen looks like she’s embalmed.
chapter-1-intro.dialogue-4: Frederick spilled food down the front of his shirt.
chapter-1-intro.dialogue-5: What a brave man you are, surviving a formal dinner!
chapter-1-intro.dialogue-6: It really is difficult, though. I can’t stand the stuffiness.
chapter-1-intro.dialogue-7: Armand didn’t remember my name. Captain Gelt had to prompt him several times.
chapter-1-intro.dialogue-8: To be fair, you started only rather recently.
chapter-1-intro.dialogue-9: Yes, I suppose it’s too much to ask. Such a complicated, burdensome thing, to remember one single name, the name of your new Alchemist.
chapter-1-intro.dialogue-10: The one who graduated at the top of his class from the College of Alchemical Engineering…
chapter-1-intro.dialogue-12: See! You remember my name just fine.
chapter-1-intro.dialogue-13: Think Armand would know my name? Keeping in mind I’ve been here my whole life.
chapter-1-intro.dialogue-14: Maybe next time you can go in my place! He might not even realize it’s a different person.
chapter-1-intro.dialogue-15: “Hnnngh, Alchemist… Provisioner… which were you again? Mm, yes, hnnnngh…”
chapter-1-intro.dialogue-17: I’ve been doing this for years.

chapter-1-outro.name: An Act of Aggression
chapter-1-outro.dialogue-0: That’s when I decided we needed to re-inventory everything in the building. You should have seen the look on Armand’s face!
chapter-1-outro.dialogue-7: I am not moping. I am merely… moodily dehjected.
chapter-1-outro.dialogue-8: And what has the great alchemist of House Van Tassen so moodily dejected?
chapter-1-outro.dialogue-9: Nothing. I mean, I’m thinking about why I’m here.
chapter-1-outro.dialogue-10: You’re here because you’re our Alchemist.
chapter-1-outro.dialogue-11: I mean in the larger sense…
chapter-1-outro.dialogue-12: The alchemist is here, isn’t he?
chapter-1-outro.dialogue-13: Captain Gelt, what can I do for you?
chapter-1-outro.dialogue-14: Your presence is required in the main hall. It’s a matter of some emergency.
chapter-1-outro.dialogue-16: An aggressive move from another House has taken us by surprise… we need to respond immediately.
chapter-1-outro.dialogue-17: My alchemy is at your disposal.
chapter-1-outro.dialogue-19: I am! Finally, something significant is happening!

chapter-2-intro.name: The Honorable Path
chapter-2-intro.dialogue-1: I will have to lodge a formal protest.
chapter-2-intro.dialogue-2: Shall I begin developing weapons for a counterattack? Something like a flame grenade with—
chapter-2-intro.dialogue-3: I doubt that will be necessary. It’s not uncommon for Houses to renegotiate territories this way.
chapter-2-intro.dialogue-4: But… they’ve taken over multiple buildings of ours without any resistance…
chapter-2-intro.dialogue-5: They’ll stop pushing forward soon and attempt to reinforce the new borders. That’s how it goes with this sort of thing.
chapter-2-intro.dialogue-6: We should push back at least a little bit.
chapter-2-intro.dialogue-7: We wouldn’t want to look weak, after all.
chapter-2-intro.dialogue-8: I’ll execute a limited rearguard action with forces stationed in the area.
chapter-2-intro.dialogue-10: Listen. House Colvan doesn’t want a full-on battle any more than we do. We’ll trade a few streets and that should be the end of it.
chapter-2-intro.dialogue-11: I believe young Taros Colvan is the head of that family now… likely he is keen to test our response.
chapter-2-intro.dialogue-12: I will send a message to him and we will settle this like honorable Houses.
chapter-2-intro.dialogue-13: Taros? He was a bright boy…
chapter-2-intro.dialogue-14: Yes. I’m sure he’ll listen to reason.

chapter-2-outro.name: Young Taros Colvan
chapter-2-outro.dialogue-0: Ha! Weaklings. You were right, Verrin. Nothing to be afraid of after all.
chapter-2-outro.dialogue-2: House Van Tassen strayed from the path for too long. And we were the agents of correction.
chapter-2-outro.dialogue-3: Now all that remains is to negotiate the terms— not that they have much of a bargaining position.
chapter-2-outro.dialogue-6: What if we just… killed them all?
chapter-2-outro.dialogue-7: That strikes me as a little extreme.
chapter-2-outro.dialogue-8: I hate the idea of this ancient weak family hanging around even after we’ve won. They’ll stick around, begging for our scraps, waxing on about the old days.
chapter-2-outro.dialogue-9: It poses a risk. And you told me yourself, Verrin, that the old ways were due for a change.
chapter-2-outro.dialogue-12: Easy enough for you to propose the idea of attacking, but when it comes time to follow all the way through…
chapter-2-outro.dialogue-13: I am absolutely not afraid! If you believe eliminating the Van Tassen line is the right choice, then I will follow.
chapter-2-outro.dialogue-14: Verrin, you consider yourself clever. But just because you’re the House alchemist doesn’t mean you can place your ideas over mine.

chapter-1-intro-doc.name: Letter of Congratulation
chapter-1-intro-doc.letter-text:
Dear Anataeus,

Congratulations on your appointment to the position of Head Alchemist to the House Van Tassen. I an very pleased to see you find a position in line with your talent and abilities.

As you prepare to leave the academic life, I want to offer a word of advice: The politics of the city are much harsher and more dangerous than those of the academy. You are a singularly gifted talent, and I would hate to see you get caught up in these conflicts.

The alchemist’s place is not to sink to the level of those around us, but to rise above them in service of our art.

Best of luck to you.
chapter-1-intro-doc.letter-attribution:
Nadine Tolomeo
Professor and Chair
College of Alchemical Engineering
Imperial University
